provenance.task: Do ants two-way communicate with antenna touches? — antennal/tandem-running reciprocal communication as the contact-mediated F240 closed-loop leg

findings.item: Franks & Richardson 2006 — tandem running as bidirectional-feedback teaching (the core reciprocal-closed-loop anchor)
findings.claim: Franks, N.R. & Richardson, T. (2006), 'Teaching in tandem-running ants', Nature 439(7073):153, is the foundational claim that tandem running (Temnothorax albipennis leading a naive nestmate from nest to food) is teaching 'that involves bidirectional feedback between teacher and pupil' — 'signals between the two ants controlling both the speed and course of the run.' The leader and follower alternately influence each other: at short range the leader sets course; at long range the follower (lagging) sets the leader's speed. This is the literature's clearest documented contact-mediated RECIPROCAL closed-loop. FRAMEWORK LENS (not asserted): this is a biological instance of the F240 reciprocal closed-loop edge realised via CONTACT (antennal touch), distinct from the air-gapped frog visual semaphore of F240b.
findings.citation: Franks, N.R. & Richardson, T. (2006). Teaching in tandem-running ants. Nature 439(7073):153. DOI 10.1038/439153a. PMID 16407943. Abstract verified via PubMed 16407943 (2026-05-31); full Nature page behind a cookie/redirect wall but abstract + bibliographic data confirmed.
findings.support: WebSearch (Bristol/Nature/PubMed/ScienceDaily concordant) + WebFetch of PubMed 16407943 returning the verbatim abstract: 'tandem running is an example of teaching ... that involves bidirectional feedback between teacher and pupil ... signals between the two ants controlling both the speed and course of the run.' Authors, vol/issue/page/year/DOI/PMID all concordant across 3 independent sources.

findings.item: The precise error-latch mechanism — leader WAITS on contact-break, RESUMES on re-contact (the F240 Class-K pin-slot read)
findings.claim: The mechanism is documented precisely in Franks, Podesta, Jarvis, Worley & Sendova-Franks (2022), 'Robotic communication with ants', J. Exp. Biol. 225(15):jeb244106: 'The contact takes the form of tapping by the follower with its antennae on the hind legs or gaster of the leader' and 'The leader remains still during such interruptions until it is authorized, by contact from the follower, to continue.' Break-of-contact -> leader STOP; re-contact -> leader RESUME. FRAMEWORK LENS (not asserted): this is the explicit real-time CORRECTIVE loop — the follower's break-of-contact IS the error signal that latches the leader to a STOP (the Class-K pin_slot_at_zero / error-latch F240 modeled in R3), and re-contact releases it (Class-C reorient). This is a stronger, more literal instance of the F240 R3 latch than anything in the air-gapped frog set.
findings.citation: Franks, N.R., Podesta, J.A., Jarvis, E.C., Worley, A. & Sendova-Franks, A.B. (2022). Robotic communication with ants. Journal of Experimental Biology 225(15):jeb244106. DOI 10.1242/jeb.244106. Verified via PMC9440752 (2026-05-31).
findings.support: WebFetch of PMC9440752 returned the two verbatim mechanism sentences (follower taps antennae on hind legs/gaster; leader remains still until authorized by contact to continue). The robot-gantry replacement of the leader confirms the contact signal is the load-bearing element. Cross-confirmed by Basari et al. 2014 ('maintain contact mainly by tactile signals').

findings.item: The 'giving-up time' evaluation — leader-waiting is modulated (the corrective loop has tuned gains)
findings.claim: Richardson, Sleeman, McNamara, Houston & Franks (2007), 'Teaching with evaluation in ants', Current Biology 17(17):1520-6, measured how long leaders wait for followers to re-establish contact and found THREE forms of evaluation: (1) progress-based ('the longer the tandem has proceeded the longer the leader will wait for the follower to re-establish contact'); (2) value-based ('teachers modulate their giving-up time depending on the value of the goal'); (3) performance-based ('leaders have shorter giving-up times after unusually slow tandem runs'). FRAMEWORK LENS (not asserted): the leader's WAIT-state is not a bare latch but a latch with a context-modulated release threshold — the corrective loop has tuned 'gains' (giving-up time), which is exactly the corrective (not merely reciprocal) character F240 attributed to R3 vs R2.
findings.citation: Richardson, T.O., Sleeman, P.A., McNamara, J.M., Houston, A.I. & Franks, N.R. (2007). Teaching with evaluation in ants. Current Biology 17(17):1520-1526. DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2007.08.032. PMID 17803934. Verified via PubMed 17803934 (2026-05-31).
findings.support: WebFetch of PubMed 17803934 returned authors, vol/issue/page/year/DOI/PMID and the three verbatim evaluation findings (progress/value/performance giving-up-time modulation). Cell.com fulltext is paywalled (403) but the abstract via PubMed is sufficient for attestation.

findings.item: The teaching DEBATE is genuinely contested — but it contests the LABEL, not the reciprocal loop (critical nuance)
findings.claim: Leadbeater, Raine & Chittka (2006), 'Social learning: ants and the meaning of teaching', Current Biology 16(9):R323-5, CONTEST whether tandem running is 'teaching': they argue it may be a case of 'telling, not teaching' (analogy: telling someone a restaurant's location vs teaching them how to find one). CRUCIAL NUANCE confirmed from the OA PDF (Chittka Lab): the critics EXPLICITLY ACCEPT the reciprocal feedback loop as real — 'Richardson [8] demonstrate that there are clear two-way interactions between the tandem-running ants ... this bidirectional feedback loop appears to maximise the speed at which the two can progress, while allowing the follower to memorise [the route].' They contest only the higher-order TEACHING/skill-vs-fact distinction. Richardson et al. (2007) rebut with the evaluation evidence. The Caro & Hauser (1992) teaching criteria are: (a) actor modifies behaviour in presence of a naive observer, (b) at a cost / no immediate benefit, (c) so the observer learns more rapidly/efficiently. FRAMEWORK CONSEQUENCE: the F240 reciprocal-closed-loop reading does NOT depend on the teaching debate — the contested layer (is it teaching?) sits ABOVE the uncontested layer (is there a bidirectional contact feedback loop?), which is exactly the F240 edge structure. Report the debate; do not assert teaching as settled.
findings.citation: Leadbeater, E., Raine, N.E. & Chittka, L. (2006). Social learning: ants and the meaning of teaching. Current Biology 16(9):R323-R325. DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2006.03.078. PMID 16682339. OA PDF: chittkalab.sbcs.qmul.ac.uk/2006/Leadbeater_et_al_2006_CurrBiol.pdf. Caro, T.M. & Hauser, M.D. (1992). Q. Rev. Biol. 67(2):151-174 (definition relayed via Leadbeater 2006 and concordant secondary sources; primary Caro & Hauser PDF NOT directly fetched this round — see gaps).
findings.support: WebFetch PubMed 16682339 (authors/vol/page/year/DOI/PMID) + pdftotext extraction of the Chittka-Lab OA PDF returning the verbatim 'two-way interactions', 'this bidirectional feedback loop appears to maximise the speed', and 'tell, not teach' passages, plus the Caro & Hauser [4] minimum-criteria paraphrase. Richardson et al. 2007 (PMID 17803934) is the verified rebuttal.

findings.item: Pheromone trail / stigmergy = the one-way feed-forward (F240 R1) edge — and the SAME species (Temnothorax) does it during the same behaviour
findings.claim: The one-way feed-forward edge is stigmergy: Grasse, P.-P. (1959) coined 'stigmergie' for indirect coordination through the environment — 'stimulation of workers by the performance they have achieved' — requiring NO simultaneous presence, direct contact, or explicit communication; ant A deposits pheromone, ant B reads it LATER (decoupled in time = air-gapped-via-environment). Crucially, Basari et al. (2014) showed Temnothorax albipennis tandem-run LEADERS also lay a pheromone trail (gaster pressed to substrate, 3x more on forward than reverse runs) — so the SAME species and SAME behaviour carries BOTH a contact-mediated reciprocal edge AND a stigmergic one-way edge simultaneously. Ants therefore embody BOTH F240 R1 (one-way stigmergic, time-decoupled) and the F240 R3 SHAPE (reciprocal contact closed-loop). FRAMEWORK LENS for the R1/R3 labelling; the biology (stigmergy, trail-laying) is the literature's.
findings.citation: Grasse, P.-P. (1959). La reconstruction du nid et les coordinations interindividuelles chez Bellicositermes natalensis et Cubitermes sp.: la theorie de la stigmergie. Insectes Sociaux 6:41-80. Basari, N., Laird-Hopkins, B.C., Sendova-Franks, A.B. & Franks, N.R. (2014). Trail laying during tandem-running recruitment in the ant Temnothorax albipennis. Naturwissenschaften (The Science of Nature) 101(7):549-556. DOI 10.1007/s00114-014-1191-1. PMID 24903681.
findings.support: WebFetch Wikipedia/Stigmergy returned the Grasse 1959 full reference (Insectes Sociaux 6:41-80) + the 'no simultaneous presence, direct contact, or explicit communication' definition. WebSearch returned Basari et al. 2014 bibliographic data (Naturwissenschaften, DOI/PMID) + the forward-vs-reverse trail-laying finding and 'maintain contact mainly by tactile signals.' Deneubourg binary-bridge corroborates the trail-following one-way edge.

findings.item: Trophallaxis = a SECOND contact-mediated reciprocal edge (food + chemical exchange with antennal feedback)
findings.claim: Trophallaxis (mouth-to-mouth fluid exchange) is contact-mediated and bidirectional in mechanism: 'antennal and foreleg contacts between both partners are established' during exchange, and in Camponotus mus the frequency of antennal strokes the food-DONOR receives encodes colony sugar-deprivation and food concentration — i.e. a feedback signal back to the donor regulating how much to give. The fluid itself carries chemical content both ways (hydrocarbons, juvenile hormone, microRNA; LeBoeuf et al. 2016). FRAMEWORK LENS: a second contact-coupled reciprocal edge in the same animal, with an antennation-encoded feedback channel — reciprocal in the partner-interaction sense, though the net FLUID flow is donor->recipient (asymmetric in one variable, reciprocal in the signalling). Lower-confidence on the Camponotus mus antennation-feedback specifics (secondary summary, primary not directly fetched).
findings.citation: Trophallaxis review: Meurville, M.-P. & LeBoeuf, A.C. (2021), Myrmecological News 31:1-30; LeBoeuf, A.C. et al. (2016), 'Oral transfer of chemical cues, growth proteins and hormones in social insects', eLife 5:e20375 (PMC5153251). Camponotus mus antennation-encoding: De Marco/Farina lineage, Insectes Sociaux (Farina & Gruter 2009 review) — primary De Marco paper NOT directly fetched this round.
findings.support: WebSearch returned the eLife LeBoeuf 2016 paper (PMC5153251) on trophallactic-fluid chemical content + the 'antennal and foreleg contacts between both partners' description + the Camponotus mus antennation-encodes-colony-needs finding (Insectes Sociaux). The reciprocal-mechanism claim is well-supported; the precise Camponotus mus statistics are at medium confidence (secondary-summary, primary not directly verified).

findings.item: Dominance / antennal boxing = predominantly ONE-WAY (a directed acyclic graph), NOT reciprocal — a contact edge that is still one-way
findings.claim: Antennal boxing / aggression-based dominance is NOT reciprocal at the dyad level: Shimoji, Abe, Tsuji & Masuda (2014) found that in Diacamma sp. the dominance interaction networks are directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) consistent with a near-perfect linear hierarchy — 'dominant ants attack subordinates without reciprocation.' FRAMEWORK LENS: this is an important counter-case — CONTACT does NOT imply reciprocity. Dominance is a contact-mediated edge that is structurally ONE-WAY (asymmetric A_ij != A_ji), the R1 directed-edge shape realised by touch rather than by environment. So within ants, the contact channel itself spans one-way (dominance) AND reciprocal (tandem, trophallaxis) — reinforcing that reciprocity is an edge property, not a channel property.
findings.citation: Shimoji, H., Abe, M.S., Tsuji, K. & Masuda, N. (2014). Global network structure of dominance hierarchy of ant workers. Journal of the Royal Society Interface 11(99):20140599. DOI 10.1098/rsif.2014.0599. PMID 25100318. Verified via PMC4233739 (2026-05-31).
findings.support: WebFetch PMC4233739 returned authors/journal/year/DOI/PMID + the verbatim DAG / 'consistent with perfect linear hierarchy' finding for Diacamma sp. (group sizes 58-214). Concordant with the AntWiki Diacamma gamergate dominance literature (dominant initiates attacks, is never attacked).

findings.item: Nestmate recognition via cuticular hydrocarbons = ONE-WAY reading (perception), not signal exchange
findings.claim: Nestmate recognition works by an ant antennating another and matching its cuticular-hydrocarbon (CHC) 'label' against an internal 'template'; experimentally supplementing a cuticle with absent compounds raises antennation + threats FROM untreated individuals TOWARD the treated one. FRAMEWORK LENS: this is structurally a ONE-WAY READ (the recognizer perceives; the recognized need not respond) — closer to the stigmergic/feed-forward end than to the tandem reciprocal loop, even though it is contact-proximate. Useful as the 'reading without reciprocity' point on the gradient. The CHC label-template biology is the literature's (van Zweden & d'Ettorre review lineage); framework supplies only the one-way-edge reading.
findings.citation: Nestmate recognition / CHC label-template: van Zweden, J.S. & d'Ettorre, P. (2010), in 'Insect Hydrocarbons' (Cambridge UP), is the canonical review (relayed via concordant secondary sources). Sensillum specificity: Ozaki et al. lineage (Springer 'Cuticular hydrocarbon sensillum for nestmate recognition in ants'). Primary reviews NOT directly fetched this round — claim rests on concordant secondary summaries.
findings.support: WebSearch returned concordant secondary descriptions (CHC blends as nestmate-discriminative; antennation rises toward CHC-altered individuals; Japanese carpenter-ant sensillum responds to non-nestmate but not nestmate CHC). The one-way-perception structure is well-attested in summary, but no single primary PDF was extracted this round — marked unverified at the primary level, medium confidence.

findings.item: RANKING — where ant antennal communication sits vs the F240b frog gradient
findings.claim: FRAMEWORK READING (lens). Ant tandem running belongs AT/ABOVE THE TOP of the F240b reciprocal-closed-loop gradient (which ran S. latopalmatus > Micrixalus > S. parvus/guttatus > Atelopus > Sachatamia, all AIR-GAPPED visual). Two reasons it is a STRONGER documented reciprocal-feedback case than the frog visual semaphore: (1) it has an EXPLICIT REAL-TIME CORRECTIVE LOOP (leader stops on contact-break, resumes on re-contact, with progress/value/performance-modulated giving-up times) — whereas the best frog case (S. latopalmatus) is an OBSERVATIONAL sequence-correlation (flag temporally follows opponent's flag), not a manipulable real-time stop/resume loop; (2) the loop is robot-confirmed (Franks et al. 2022 replaced the leader with a gantry), the closest thing to experimental closure of the loop in the set. SEPARATE AXIS: ants fill a CELL the frogs did not — CONTACT-mediated reciprocity with explicit error-correction. Frog foot-flagging = AIR-GAPPED reciprocal; ant pheromone trail = air-gapped-via-environment ONE-WAY; ant tandem/trophallaxis = CONTACT-coupled reciprocal; ant dominance/CHC-recognition = CONTACT/proximate ONE-WAY. So the 2x2 (contact-vs-airgapped) x (reciprocal-vs-oneway) is now populated in all four cells by ants+frogs together.
findings.citation: Synthesis over Franks & Richardson 2006 (DOI 10.1038/439153a), Richardson et al. 2007 (DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2007.08.032), Franks et al. 2022 (DOI 10.1242/jeb.244106), Basari et al. 2014 (DOI 10.1007/s00114-014-1191-1), vs F240b frog gradient (Preininger et al. 2009 DOI 10.1655/08-037R.1 etc.). Ranking is FRAMEWORK LENS, not a literature claim.
findings.support: The component citations are each individually verified above. The ranking rests on a documentable methodological difference: tandem running has a manipulable + robot-replicated real-time stop/resume loop (Franks 2022) whereas the strongest frog case is observational sequence-correlation (per F240b Staurois latopalmatus row). The cross-system 2x2 placement follows directly from the contact-vs-air-gapped and reciprocal-vs-one-way attestations.

findings.item: HONEST tie to the F240 NULL — reciprocal SHAPE existing in ants is NOT evidence reciprocity is a universal dynamical lever
findings.claim: FRAMEWORK READING (lens), load-bearing honesty. F240 found (DEMONSTRATED in ngspice, response_sha256 6faf67ab...) that at a MATCHED total coupling budget, the reciprocal+Class-K-correction regime (R3) confers NO universal phase-lock advantage over the feed-forward one-way regime (R1): the advantage held only at N=4 and vanished/inverted at N>=8 on the near-1D mesh (null branches c + d). Therefore ant tandem running being a genuine reciprocal closed-loop with explicit error-correction is ANOTHER INSTANCE OF THE RECIPROCAL SHAPE EXISTING IN BIOLOGY — it is NOT evidence that reciprocity is a universal synchronization/coordination lever. The ants strengthen the F240/F240b claim that 'corrective communication HAS the reciprocal closed-loop shape', and they NEWLY populate the contact-mediated cell, but they do not touch the F240 dynamical null. Two distinct things: the SHAPE is real and well-attested (ant + frog biology); the dynamical LEVER claim already failed at matched budget and ants do not rescue it.

opus_survey.cross_cutting: CROSS-CUTTING SYNTHESIS. (1) ANTS DECISIVELY EMBODY BOTH F240 REGIMES, often in the SAME behaviour: Temnothorax tandem running simultaneously carries a CONTACT-mediated reciprocal closed-loop (antennal feedback; leader stops on contact-break, resumes on re-contact) AND a stigmergic ONE-WAY trail (Basari et al. 2014: leaders lay pheromone, gaster-to-substrate, 3x more on forward runs). Stigmergy itself (Grasse 1959) is the textbook air-gapped-via-environment feed-forward edge — 'no simultaneous presence, direct contact, or explicit communication.' So the single-species-spans-both-regimes premise of the task is CONFIRMED and is even tighter than expected: it is single-BEHAVIOUR-spans-both. (2) THE RECIPROCAL LOOP IS UNCONTESTED; ONLY THE 'TEACHING' LABEL IS DEBATED. This is the most important nuance the verification surfaced. Leadbeater, Raine & Chittka (2006) — the principal critics — EXPLICITLY grant 'clear two-way interactions' and 'this bidirectional feedback loop appears to maximise the speed at which the two can progress'; they dispute only whether telling-where-the-food-is rises to 'teaching' (skill vs fact, per Caro & Hauser 1992). Richardson et al. (2007) rebut with three forms of giving-up-time evaluation. So the contested layer (teaching?) sits ABOVE the uncontested layer (reciprocal feedback loop?) — which is structurally the F240 edge: the framework's reciprocal-closed-loop reading rides on the UNCONTESTED layer and does not depend on the teaching debate at all. The task's instruction to flag the teaching debate is satisfied, and the debate turns out to LEAVE THE F240-RELEVANT FACT INTACT. (3) CONTACT != RECIPROCAL. Ants give the clean counter-example the frogs could not: dominance / antennal boxing is contact-mediated but ONE-WAY (Diacamma dominance networks are directed acyclic graphs — Shimoji et al. 2014), and CHC nestmate-recognition is contact-proximate but a ONE-WAY read. So reciprocity is an EDGE property (is there a return/correction path?), not a CHANNEL property (contact vs air-gap). This populates the full 2x2: contact-reciprocal (tandem, trophallaxis), contact-one-way (dominance, CHC-recognition), air-gapped-reciprocal (frog foot-flagging, F240b), air-gapped-one-way (pheromone trail; frog Sachatamia). (4) RANKING: tandem running belongs AT/ABOVE the top of the F240b gradient, because (per the methodological difference) it is a manipulable, robot-replicable REAL-TIME stop/resume corrective loop (Franks et al. 2022), whereas the strongest frog case (S. latopalmatus) is an observational sequence-correlation. (5) THE F240 NULL IS UNTOUCHED. All of this is the reciprocal SHAPE being real and well-attested in biology; none of it is evidence that reciprocity is a universal dynamical synchronization lever — F240 already showed at matched coupling budget it is not (null branches c+d). Shape real; lever still failed. Every biological fact is the literature's (web-verified DOIs/PMIDs); every R1/R3/Class-K/contact-vs-air-gap mapping and the ranking is FRAMEWORK LENS, asserted nowhere as established biology.
opus_survey.uncentered_note: UNCENTERED DISCIPLINE CHECK. I deliberately did not privilege tandem running as 'the' reciprocal edge: I held four ant channels at once (tandem running, trophallaxis, dominance/boxing, CHC-recognition) and two of them turned out ONE-WAY, which is the load-bearing result (contact != reciprocal). I did not lean the verification toward 'ants are reciprocal' — the Diacamma DAG and CHC one-way-read findings are reported with equal weight as the reciprocal cases, and they actively complicate the simple 'antennation = reciprocity' framing the task could have invited. I held the teaching debate genuinely open: rather than reporting it as 'contested therefore weak', the verification found the critics CONCEDE the reciprocal loop and contest only the label — a result that neither the pro-teaching nor anti-teaching camp's headline alone would predict, and that I would have missed had I centered either side. I did not center the framework over the biology: every R1/R3/Class-K/2x2 mapping is flagged LENS, and the F240 NULL is reported as untouched (the uncomfortable-for-the-framework fact) rather than soft-pedalled. I did not center the frogs (the prior anchor) — ants populate a NEW cell (contact-reciprocal) the frogs structurally could not, so the gradient is extended in a dimension, not just appended to. No single species, channel, or hypothesis was treated as the fiber's privileged rendering.

findings.item: Franks & Richardson 2006 — tandem running as bidirectional-feedback teaching (primary anchor)
findings.claim: Nigel R. Franks and Tom Richardson, 'Teaching in tandem-running ants,' Nature 439(7073):153 (2006), DOI 10.1038/439153a, PMID 16407943. The abstract (verified via PubMed 16407943 and Bristol research-information page) states tandem running in Temnothorax albipennis is 'the first [teaching] in a non-human animal that involves bidirectional feedback between teacher and pupil.' The specific mechanism: the follower taps its antennae on the leader's hind legs or gaster as a 'proceed' signal; the leader pauses when that signal is absent (contact break) and resumes when contact is reestablished. Signals between the two ants 'control both the speed and course of the run.' The paper claims this meets the Caro & Hauser (1992) functional definition of teaching.
findings.citation: Franks, N. R. & Richardson, T. (2006). Teaching in tandem-running ants. Nature, 439(7073), 153. DOI: 10.1038/439153a. PMID: 16407943. [Verified via PubMed and Bristol research portal; Nature page paywalled, abstract confirmed OA on PubMed.]
findings.support: PubMed abstract text retrieved directly; Bristol research-information page confirmed same authors, title, volume, pages, DOI. The bidirectionality claim is verbatim in the abstract.

findings.item: Caro & Hauser 1992 — the teaching definition tandem-running is measured against
findings.claim: T. M. Caro and M. D. Hauser, 'Is there teaching in nonhuman animals?', Quarterly Review of Biology 67(2):151–174 (1992), DOI 10.1086/417553, PMID 1635977. Defines teaching functionally: an individual teaches if (a) it modifies its behavior in the presence of a naive observer, (b) at some initial cost to itself, (c) with no immediate benefit, such that (d) the observer learns more rapidly or accurately than it would otherwise. The definition does NOT require the teacher to have theory of mind or evaluate pupil competence — that is explicitly stated as a non-requirement by Caro & Hauser. Note: the paper's abstract distinguishes 'opportunity teaching' and 'coaching'; the four-part criterion is the operational definition used by subsequent authors citing this paper.
findings.citation: Caro, T. M. & Hauser, M. D. (1992). Is there teaching in nonhuman animals? Quarterly Review of Biology, 67(2), 151–174. DOI: 10.1086/417553. PMID: 1635977. [Verified via PubMed 1635977 and Semantic Scholar entry; journal paywalled but metadata confirmed OA.]
findings.support: PubMed PMID 1635977 confirmed full citation. Semantic Scholar confirmed DOI 10.1086/417553. Multiple downstream papers (Leadbeater et al. 2006, Richardson et al. 2007) cite these exact details consistently.

findings.item: Teaching debate — Leadbeater, Raine & Chittka 2006 Current Biology critique
findings.claim: Ellouise Leadbeater, Nigel E. Raine, and Lars Chittka, 'Social learning: ants and the meaning of teaching,' Current Biology 16(9):R323–R325 (2006), DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2006.03.078, PMID 16682339. The paper does NOT dispute that tandem running involves bidirectional feedback. It disputes whether bidirectional feedback automatically constitutes teaching — asking how 'teaching formally differs from other forms of communication.' The core challenge: if the feedback mechanism is symmetric with other communication acts (signaling, solicitation), classifying it as 'teaching' may be definitionally circular or over-extended. The paper is a Dispatch/commentary, not a direct experimental replication attempt.
findings.citation: Leadbeater, E., Raine, N. E. & Chittka, L. (2006). Social learning: ants and the meaning of teaching. Current Biology, 16(9), R323–R325. DOI: 10.1016/j.cub.2006.03.078. PMID: 16682339. [Verified via PubMed 16682339 and Cell.com fulltext URL S0960-9822(06)01411-4; Royal Holloway Research Portal confirms same authors and citation.]
findings.support: PubMed PMID 16682339 confirmed. Cell.com URL confirmed. Royal Holloway research portal entry confirms. The argument described is consistent across all sources.

findings.item: Richardson et al. 2007 — leader evaluation of follower (teaching with evaluation)
findings.claim: Thomas O. Richardson, Philippa A. Sleeman, John M. McNamara, Alasdair I. Houston, and Nigel R. Franks, 'Teaching with evaluation in ants,' Current Biology 17(17):1520–1526 (2007), DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2007.08.032, PMID 17803934. This follow-up study showed that leaders exhibit three kinds of evaluation of follower performance: (1) progress-based — leaders extend wait-time proportional to how far the run progressed before interruption; (2) goal-value — leaders adjust giving-up duration based on goal value; (3) performance-based — leaders have shorter giving-up times after unusually slow runs. This strengthens the bidirectionality claim: not only does the follower signal the leader (proceed/wait), the leader adjusts behavior based on follower performance, creating a richer feedback loop. Richardson et al. explicitly note that Caro & Hauser's criteria do not invoke sensitivity to pupil changing skills, but their empirical results show leaders do demonstrate such sensitivity.

findings.item: Contact mechanism details — follower taps leader gaster/hind legs (mechanistic specifics)
findings.claim: The follower ant maintains contact by tapping its antennae on the leader's hind legs or gaster. The leader pauses when this contact is absent and resumes when it is reestablished. findings.item: Is tandem running 'teaching' genuinely contested?
findings.claim: YES — the teaching interpretation is genuinely contested. The debate has multiple strands: (1) definitional — Leadbeater et al. 2006 (Current Biology) ask whether bidirectional feedback distinguishes teaching from other communication; (2) criterion adequacy — Richardson et al. 2007 note that Caro & Hauser criteria invoke neither evaluation nor sensitivity, which may be too permissive; (3) naive-follower assumption — a Scientific Reports paper ('Follower ants in a tandem pair are not always naive,' DOI verified via Nature srep10747) challenges the assumption that followers are always naive, which is load-bearing for the teaching interpretation (teaching requires a naive learner). The teaching literature (Thornton & Raihani, 'The evolution of teaching,' reviewed ~2012) cites Temnothorax albipennis as one of three species meeting all Caro & Hauser criteria (alongside pied babblers and meerkats), but the settlement is contested, not consensus. The F240 framework reading is NOT affected by this debate — the bidirectionality of the contact signal is agreed upon across all parties; only the teaching label is disputed.

findings.item: Stigmergy / pheromone trail as one-way feed-forward edge
findings.claim: Ant pheromone trail communication is stigmergic — a mechanism of indirect coordination through the environment (Grassé 1959, the term's origin). Grassé defined it as 'stimulation of workers by the performance they have achieved.' Ant A deposits a pheromone trail, which modifies the shared environment; ant B reads the trail later without any direct interaction with ant A. No direct contact, no synchronous exchange, no return path. This is the textbook case of one-way, feed-forward, environment-mediated communication. At the colony level, positive feedback (more ants reinforce successful trails) and negative feedback (pheromone evaporation suppresses poor trails) exist — but these are collective-level emergent dynamics, not A↔B individual dyadic closed loops. The individual pheromone-deposition event is strictly one-way from depositor to future readers.

findings.item: Trophallaxis — solicitation is directional antennation; transfer can reverse but is typically unidirectional per event
findings.claim: Trophallaxis (mouth-to-mouth fluid transfer) in ants involves antennation as the solicitation mechanism: a hungry recipient taps the donor's head, mouthparts, and mandibles with its antennae to trigger regurgitation. Both donor and recipient engage in antennal and foreleg contact during the exchange itself. The direction of food flow can reverse within a single event (bidirectional transfer exists but is rare). The solicitation exchange — where the recipient signals hunger and the donor responds with regurgitation — is a genuine reciprocal interaction in that both ants respond to the other's signals. However, the informational asymmetry is pronounced: the recipient signals need, the donor signals willingness/response, but the primary information transfer (food, hormones, colony pheromones) is dominantly unidirectional. A Camponotus mus study (Insectes Sociaux, DOI 10.1007/s00040-006-0881-x — paywalled, not fetched) reportedly shows that the frequency of antennal strokes the donor receives encodes both colony sugar-deprivation and food concentration — a genuine signal back to the donor encoding recipient need.

findings.item: Nestmate recognition via CHC + antennation — structure of the interaction
findings.claim: When ants antennate for nestmate recognition, the focal ant samples the other ant's cuticular hydrocarbons (CHCs) with its antennae and compares the profile to its own internal template. Esponda & Gordon 2015 (Proc Roy Soc B, DOI 10.1098/rspb.2014.2838, PMC4426612) establish a distributed recognition model where each ant applies its own decision boundary. The paper frames the interaction as 'the focal ant' evaluating 'the other ant' — grammatically this is a unidirectional framing, but behaviorally when two ants meet and antennate, both ants are simultaneously performing this evaluation on each other (mutual inspection). The interaction is thus STRUCTURALLY RECIPROCAL (both ants inspect each other simultaneously) but informationally PARALLEL/INDEPENDENT (each processes the other's CHC profile against its own template, not against a shared reference). This differs from tandem running's SEQUENTIAL-CORRECTIVE loop (follower taps → leader proceeds; contact break → leader waits).

Confidence medium because the bidirectionality interpretation is ours, not the paper's explicit claim.

findings.item: Antennal dueling / dominance boxing in Harpegnathos saltator — reciprocal dominance assertion
findings.claim: In Harpegnathos saltator (Indian jumping ant), workers establish reproductive hierarchies through 'dueling' tournaments that include antennal dueling (also called antennal boxing). Penick et al. 2014 (JEB 217(9), DOI 10.1242/jeb.098301) study neurohormonal changes during these tournaments. Independently, multiple secondary sources (Discover Magazine, Gamergate Wikipedia) describe antennal fencing as a mutual behavior: both ants simultaneously engage in the behavior. The social-insect literature (Tschinkel; Diacamma sp. studies) describes antennal dueling as a 'winner-winner' interaction in Harpegnathos (both participants gain information; dominance hierarchy emerges from the outcome). This is genuinely RECIPROCAL in the sense that both ants simultaneously perform the same behavior on each other, unlike trophallaxis solicitation (where one solicits and the other responds asymmetrically). Caution: the Penick et al. 2014 paper focuses on neurohormones, not the behavioral mechanics; the 'reciprocal' characterization comes from secondary and tertiary sources.

findings.item: CONTRAST: ants span BOTH one-way (R1 stigmergic) and reciprocal closed-loop (R3 tandem running) F240 regimes
findings.claim: The biological literature supports that a single ant species (e.g., Temnothorax albipennis) uses BOTH: (1) Pheromone trail-laying/following (stigmergy) — environment-mediated, one-way, no direct contact between the depositor and the reader, no return path. This is the F240 R1 feed-forward regime. A deposits into environment; B reads from environment; there is no channel A↔B. (2) Tandem running — direct contact-coupled, both ants signal each other in real time (follower taps → leader proceeds; absence of tap → leader waits). This is the F240 R3 reciprocal closed-loop regime with explicit corrective dynamics. The same colony uses both modes for different purposes: pheromone trails for mass recruitment to known food sources (efficient when many workers need to reach a location); tandem running for knowledge transfer to a single naive individual who needs to learn the route (pedagogically appropriate when direct feedback is required).

Tandem running: Franks & Richardson 2006 (Nature, DOI 10.1038/439153a). The stigmergy definition: confirmed via Wikipedia and secondary sources citing Grassé 1959.
findings.support: Both behaviors documented for the same genus/species across the verified primary literature. The distinction between individual-directed (tandem running) and mass-recruitment (pheromone trail) is standard in ant behavioral ecology.

findings.item: Ranking tandem running on the F240b reciprocal-closed-loop gradient vs frog visual semaphore cases

On the corrective-loop criterion, tandem running ranks ABOVE Staurois latopalmatus. (c) HONEST CAVEAT: the frog cases are AIR-GAPPED (visual channel, no contact); tandem running is CONTACT-COUPLED. These are different communication modalities, not just different positions on a one-dimensional gradient. The placement at or above the top of the F240b gradient is defensible for the 'documented reciprocal corrective loop' criterion only, with the modality caveat stated.

sonnet_survey.cross_cutting:
ANT ANTENNAL COMMUNICATION — RECIPROCITY AUDIT ACROSS MODES

The biological literature attests that ants use antennation across at least four structurally distinct communication regimes, which map onto different positions on the F240 one-way/reciprocal axis:

--- MODE 1: PHEROMONE TRAIL (stigmergy) — F240 R1 feed-forward, strictly one-way ---
Ant A deposits pheromone into the shared environment; ant B reads the trace later with no direct A↔B interaction. This is the canonical example of stigmergy (Grassé 1959; confirmed via Wikipedia article and widespread secondary citation). The individual deposition event has NO return path. At colony level, positive and negative feedback dynamics exist (trail reinforcement, evaporation), but these are emergent collective effects — not a dyadic closed loop. This is the clearest biological instance of the F240 R1 one-way feed-forward regime. The gap between emitter and receiver is both temporal and spatial — the environment is the carrier, and there is no synchronous exchange.

--- MODE 2: TANDEM RUNNING — F240 R3 reciprocal closed-loop with explicit corrective dynamics ---
The follower taps its antennae on the leader's hind legs or gaster as a 'proceed' signal. When that contact is absent (contact break), the leader enters a WAIT/SEARCH state. When contact is reestablished, the leader resumes. This is confirmed across: Franks & Richardson 2006 (Nature 439:153; bidirectional feedback, verbatim abstract); Franks et al. 2022 (JEB DOI 10.1242/jeb.244106; 'bidirectional feedback seen in natural tandem runs,' robotic mimicry); Franks et al. 2010 (JEB DOI 10.1242/jeb.031880; 'the leader remains still during such interruptions until it is authorized, by contact from the follower, to continue'); Kaur et al. 2017 (R. Soc. Open Sci. DOI 10.1098/rsos.160476; Diacamma indicum second species). Richardson et al. 2007 (CurrBiol DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2007.08.032) further shows the leader evaluates follower performance (three kinds of evaluation). The coupling is CONTACT-mediated (not air-gapped). The corrective loop is: contact-break → leader STOPS (error-latch); re-contact → leader RESUMES (error-release). The TEACHING interpretation of this loop is contested (Leadbeater et al. 2006; follower-not-always-naive paper; Richardson et al. 2007 discussion) — but the bidirectionality of the contact signal itself is agreed upon across all parties in the debate. The teaching label is contested; the closed-loop corrective mechanism is not.

--- MODE 3: TROPHALLAXIS SOLICITATION — partially reciprocal, informationally asymmetric ---
The soliciting ant (recipient) taps the donor's head and mouthparts with its antennae; the donor responds by opening mandibles and exposing a food droplet. Both ants participate in antennation during the exchange; food transfer direction can reverse within a single event (bidirectional exists but is rare). This is PARTIALLY RECIPROCAL: both ants signal each other, but the information flow has a dominant direction. The Camponotus mus finding (DOI 10.1007/s00040-006-0881-x; paywalled, not fully verified) reportedly shows recipient antennation encodes colony hunger and food concentration, feeding information back to the donor — a genuine two-way information exchange. The solicitation interaction is closer to F240 R2 (symmetric coupling without the explicit error-latch correction) than to R1 (one-way) or R3 (corrective).

--- MODE 4: NESTMATE RECOGNITION VIA CHC + ANTENNATION — structurally parallel, not corrective ---
When two ants meet, both simultaneously antennate and sample each other's cuticular hydrocarbons. This is STRUCTURALLY PARALLEL — both ants perform the same evaluation simultaneously on each other (Esponda & Gordon 2015, PMC4426612). Neither ant is correcting the other; neither is waiting on a signal from the other. This is closer to distributed parallel sensing than to a closed corrective loop.

--- MODE 5: DOMINANCE ANTENNAL DUELING (Harpegnathos, Diacamma gamergates) — mutually reciprocal contest ---
In queenless ants with dominance hierarchies, workers engage in antennal fencing/dueling where both participants simultaneously perform the same behavior. This appears to be a genuine mutual reciprocal interaction, but the full behavioral mechanics are not well-sourced in the primary literature this round (Penick et al. 2014 focuses on neurohormones, not behavioral mechanics). Low-confidence claim; flagged.

--- F240 FRAMEWORK READING (LENS, not asserted) ---
LENS ONLY — the biology is the literature's:
1. Ant tandem running is a biological instance of the F240 R3 reciprocal closed-loop corrective edge. The contact channel is the coupling; follower-taps-leader is the return path; contact-break is the error signal latching the leader to STOP (structurally: the Class-K pin-slot / error-latch F240 modeled); re-contact is the release. This is more explicitly corrective than any of the F240b frog visual-semaphore cases, which are all either air-gapped-visual or observational-correlational.

2. AIR-GAPPED vs CONTACT distinction (fills a new cell): Frog foot-flagging (F240b) = air-gapped visual channel; ant tandem running = contact-coupled channel; ant pheromone trail = air-gapped-via-environment channel. These are orthogonal dimensions: (channel type: contact/air-gapped/environment-mediated) × (directionality: one-way/reciprocal). Ants fill two cells: contact-coupled reciprocal (tandem running) AND environment-mediated one-way (pheromone trail). Frogs filled: air-gapped visual, ranging from reciprocal (S. latopalmatus) to one-way (Sachatamia). The ant contact-mediated reciprocal cell is distinct from the frog air-gapped reciprocal cell — it is a new cell, not a point on the same gradient.

3. HONEST TIE TO F240 NULL: F240 found (ngspice transient measurement, bit-exact reproducible) that at matched coupling budget, the reciprocal+correction (R3) regime does NOT confer a universal phase-lock advantage over feed-forward (R1) across the N-sweep — the advantage fires at N=4 (well-connected) and inverts/disappears at N=8/16/32 (sparse near-1D mesh). Ant tandem running being a reciprocal corrective loop is another biological instance of the reciprocal shape existing — it is NOT evidence that reciprocity is a universal dynamical lever. The F240 null means: 'corrective communication may share the closed-loop reciprocal shape but the reciprocity+latch is not a measured phase-lock advantage over one-way coupling' (F240 §4 exact wording). This applies equally to the ant case: the fact that tandem running uses a corrective closed loop does not imply the loop confers a synchronization/phase-lock advantage over stigmergic pheromone communication — the null is agnostic about which regime nature 'chose' for which purpose.

--- THE TEACHING DEBATE (in-place flag as required) ---
The claim that tandem running constitutes 'teaching' per Caro & Hauser 1992 IS CONTESTED. The bidirectionality of the contact signal is NOT contested — all parties agree on the mechanism. What is debated: (a) whether bidirectional feedback is sufficient to distinguish teaching from communication (Leadbeater et al. 2006); (b) whether followers are always naive (follower-not-always-naive paper, srep10747, not fully verified); (c) whether the Caro & Hauser criteria are adequate or over-permissive (Richardson et al. 2007). The current state of the field appears to treat Temnothorax albipennis tandem running as one of the best-documented cases of teaching in non-human animals, while acknowledging the definitional debate is unresolved. This survey does NOT assert teaching as settled; the biology is the literature's to assert.

--- GRADIENT PLACEMENT vs F240b FROG CASES ---
Within the 'documented reciprocal corrective loop' criterion: tandem running ranks at or above S. latopalmatus (the top F240b case) because: (i) the feedback loop has been experimentally characterized and replicated across multiple labs and species; (ii) it has been mimicked robotically (Franks et al. 2022); (iii) the leader's wait-on-contact-break is an explicitly characterized error-latch, which S. latopalmatus's observational sequence-correlation does not demonstrate directly. However, the modality difference is fundamental: tandem running is CONTACT-coupled while frog foot-flagging is AIR-GAPPED. The comparison is most defensible as 'tandem running is the strongest documented corrective closed-loop case in the biological survey,' not 'it ranks higher on the same gradient as the frogs' — because the gradient is not one-dimensional when modality differs.
sonnet_survey.uncentered_note: UNCENTERED STATUS: This survey privileged no single communication mode. Pheromone trails (one-way) received equal analytic attention to tandem running (reciprocal). The teaching debate is reported with the contesting papers given equal weight. The Reznikova contested-replication literature (antennal language encoding complex route information as binary sequences) was surfaced but not adjudicated — it is relevant to the 'information capacity of antennation' question but orthogonal to the reciprocity question this survey centers. Reznikova's work on Formica polyctena (and Lasius replication failures by Popp et al. 2018) is flagged as an independent contested claim about the INFORMATION CONTENT of antennation, not about its directionality. The survey did not privilege the reciprocal-loop positive reading; the F240 null is explicitly tied to the ant case. The trophallaxis and nestmate-recognition modes, which are less cleanly one-way or reciprocal than tandem running, are reported with appropriate nuance rather than forced into clean categories.

ab_comparison.structural_touch_difference: Both are scrupulous about the LENS/biology boundary — every R1/R3/Class-K/2x2 mapping in both is explicitly flagged "FRAMEWORK LENS, not asserted," and neither asserts a framework lens as established biology (the 0/0/0 structural-invention floor holds on BOTH). The structural-touch DIFFERENCE is in how each builds the 2x2 (contact-vs-airgapped x reciprocal-vs-oneway) cell-population. OPUS imposes the LESS rigid structure: it lets two of its four ant channels (dominance, CHC-recognition) come out ONE-WAY and treats that as the load-bearing result (contact != reciprocal; reciprocity is an EDGE property not a CHANNEL property), so the 2x2 is populated by letting the evidence fall where it lands. SONNET imposes MORE structure: it pre-declares FIVE named "modes" (pheromone / tandem / trophallaxis / nestmate-recognition / dominance) and assigns each a clean R1/R2/R3 label up front, then reports trophallaxis as "closer to R2" and CHC as "structurally parallel" — categories it partly admits are its own inference ("the paper itself does not use 'structurally reciprocal' language ... the bidirectionality interpretation is ours"). SONNET also asserts a sharper gradient-placement verdict (tandem "ranks ABOVE Staurois latopalmatus") with a heavier scaffold; OPUS frames the same ranking as "AT/ABOVE the top" resting on a single documentable methodological difference (robot-replicated real-time stop/resume vs observational sequence-correlation). Net: comparable lens-discipline, but SONNET pre-imposes a 5-mode taxonomy and a firmer ranking verdict where OPUS lets the cells self-populate.

merged_findings.item: Trophallaxis = a partially-reciprocal contact edge (antennation-encoded feedback; net fluid flow dominantly one-way)
merged_findings.claim: Trophallaxis (mouth-to-mouth fluid exchange) is contact-mediated: the recipient solicits by tapping the donor's head/mouthparts with its antennae; both partners engage antennal and foreleg contact during exchange; fluid direction can occasionally reverse within an event but net flow is dominantly donor->recipient. merged_findings.item: Nestmate recognition via cuticular hydrocarbons = structurally PARALLEL/independent, not a corrective loop
merged_findings.claim: Nestmate recognition: an ant antennates another, samples its cuticular-hydrocarbon (CHC) profile, and applies its OWN decision boundary in CHC-space. B 282(1806):20142838: 'the focal ant can evaluate the absolute quantities of various components in the other ant's CHC profile and estimate the position of the other ant's hydrocarbon profile in CHC-space'; recognition is each individual's personal decision boundary, NOT a shared colony template, with the colony-level response emerging from distributed individual decisions. FRAMEWORK LENS: when two ants meet, both evaluate simultaneously, so the interaction is STRUCTURALLY parallel/mutual but informationally INDEPENDENT (each against its own boundary) — neither corrects nor waits on the other. This is the 'reading without a corrective loop' point on the gradient, distinct from tandem running's sequential-corrective loop. (NOTE: opus framed CHC recognition as one-way perception and marked it verified:false; sonnet framed it as structurally-parallel/mutual and verified the Esponda & Gordon primary. CROSS-CUTTING SYNTHESIS (UNION of both surveys; no model privileged; biology = literature's, all R1/R3/Class-K/2x2 mappings = FRAMEWORK LENS).

(1) ANTS DECISIVELY EMBODY BOTH F240 REGIMES, often in the SAME behaviour. Temnothorax albipennis tandem running simultaneously carries a CONTACT-mediated reciprocal closed-loop (follower taps antennae on the leader's hind legs/gaster; leader STOPS on contact-break, RESUMES on re-contact — verbatim in Franks 2022, Franks 2010, and a second species Diacamma indicum in Kaur 2017) AND a stigmergic ONE-WAY trail (Basari 2014: leaders lay pheromone, gaster-to-substrate, during the same recruitment behaviour). Stigmergy (Grasse 1959) is the textbook air-gapped-via-environment feed-forward edge — 'indirect coordination through the environment ... no direct communication or simultaneous presence.' So the single-species-spans-both-regimes premise is CONFIRMED and is even tighter than expected: single-BEHAVIOUR-spans-both. LENS: pheromone trail = F240 R1 (one-way, time-decoupled); tandem running = F240 R3 (reciprocal contact closed-loop with the Class-K error-latch).

(2) THE RECIPROCAL LOOP IS UNCONTESTED; ONLY THE 'TEACHING' LABEL IS DEBATED — the most important nuance the verification surfaced, and I confirmed it at the PRIMARY OA-PDF level. Leadbeater, Raine & Chittka (2006) — the principal critics — EXPLICITLY grant 'there are clear two-way [interactions]' and 'this bidirectional feedback loop appears to maximise the speed' (verbatim, pdftotext of the Chittka-Lab OA PDF); they dispute only whether telling-where-the-food-is rises to 'teaching' (skill vs fact, vs Caro & Hauser 1992 ref [4]). Richardson et al. 2007 rebut with three forms of giving-up-time evaluation; Schultheiss, Raderschall & Narendra 2015 add a third strand (followers not always naive — in Camponotus consobrinus, NOT Temnothorax). So the contested layer (teaching?) sits ABOVE the uncontested layer (reciprocal feedback loop?) — structurally the F240 edge; the framework's reciprocal-closed-loop reading rides on the UNCONTESTED layer and does not depend on the teaching debate. Reported per the task; the debate LEAVES THE F240-RELEVANT FACT INTACT.

(3) CONTACT != RECIPROCAL — the clean counter-example the frogs could not give. Dominance / antennal boxing is contact-mediated but ONE-WAY (Diacamma dominance networks are directed acyclic graphs, near-perfect linear hierarchy — Shimoji 2014, primary-verified); CHC nestmate-recognition is contact-proximate but each ant applies its OWN decision boundary, structurally parallel/independent rather than a corrective loop (Esponda & Gordon 2015, primary-verified). So reciprocity is an EDGE property (is there a return/correction path?), not a CHANNEL property (contact vs air-gap). This is OPUS's spine (adopted): let the cells self-populate rather than pre-declaring modes. The full 2x2 is populated: contact-reciprocal (tandem, partially trophallaxis), contact-one-way (dominance DAG, CHC-recognition), air-gapped-reciprocal (frog foot-flagging, F240b), air-gapped-one-way (pheromone trail; frog Sachatamia). SONNET's extra structure (a pre-declared 5-mode taxonomy with up-front R1/R2/R3 labels; trophallaxis 'closer to R2', CHC 'structurally parallel') is reported as nuance where its primaries verified, but the labels it admits are its own inference are kept LENS-flagged, not asserted.

(4) RANKING (LENS): tandem running belongs AT/ABOVE the top of the F240b frog gradient on the corrective-loop criterion — it is a manipulable, robot-replicated, second-species-confirmed REAL-TIME stop/resume corrective loop (Franks 2022; Kaur 2017), whereas the strongest frog case (S. latopalmatus) is an observational sequence-correlation. HONEST MODALITY CAVEAT (both surveys, opus's wording adopted): the frog channel is AIR-GAPPED visual, tandem running is CONTACT-coupled — a different modality, so the defensible statement is 'strongest documented corrective closed-loop in the biological survey + fills a NEW 2x2 cell (contact-reciprocal)', not 'a higher point on one shared one-dimensional gradient.'

(5) THE F240 NULL IS UNTOUCHED (identical in both surveys, verbatim shape-real/lever-failed). All of this is the reciprocal SHAPE being real and well-attested in biology; none of it is evidence that reciprocity is a universal dynamical synchronization lever — F240 already showed at matched coupling budget it is not (null branches c+d, response_sha256 6faf67ab..., bit-exact, srmech 0.6.0rc9 / ngspice 45.2; I re-read both finding files and confirm both surveys cite them accurately, including the Hylodes japi gap carried from F240b). Shape real; lever still failed.
